learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. The petitioner is before this Court seeking regular bail in Crime No.18/2023 of respondent Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 498-A of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").

Brief facts of the case:
3. The brother of the deceased lodged a complaint stating that the petitioner married his sister 12 to 13 years ago.
The couple had three children, two male children and one female child.
Both the deceased and the petitioner were doing coolie work for their livelihood.
On 21.01.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the complainant received a message through his younger brother that the petitioner killed his wife and went away from the house.
Immediately, the complainant and other elders of the area accompanied him and came to place where the deceased was living.
They NC: 2024:KHC-D:9642 saw that the deceased was lying on the floor with pool of blood and also noticed that the sickle (Koita) was also found near the dead body.

The petitioner was not found near the house, however,
the children were there.
On enquiry, the children told that, the petitioner had killed his wife and went away from the spot.
Based on the information, the complainant lodged a complaint against the petitioner.
The jurisdictional Police have registered a case in crime No.18/2023 for the offence under Sections 498-A and 302 of IPC.
After conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is a love marriage and the petitioner liked her very much and married her.
Couple had blessed with three children and they were living happily in the shed.
None of the witnesses have witnessed the alleged incident.
However, the Police have implicated the petitioner falsely even though he was not present at the spot at the time of NC: 2024:KHC-D:9642 alleged incident had taken place.
The petitioner is the sole earning member of the family and all the children are depending on the income of the petitioner.
If he is kept in judicial custody, they become orphans.
The petitioner will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, learned counsel for the petitioner, prays to allow the bail application.

5. Per contra, learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that there are eye witnesses to the incident and they are all consistent in their statement that the petitioner had killed Udachappa S/O Neelappa Devarmani vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74108925/

sentences.text: his wife, children are also eye witnesses to the incident.
If he is released on bail, there may be a threat to the children and there may be chances of absconding from the case.
Making such submission, learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears from the record that the complainant NC: 2024:KHC-D:9642 lodged a complaint based on the information received by him through third persons.
There are some inconsistencies in the statements of the children regarding the presence of the petitioner at the spot at the time of alleged incident.
None of the witnesses have noticed his presence in the house at the time of the incident and even after the incident.
Merely because he was not present at the spot, after the incident, that may not be a ground to suspect his involvement in the said murder.
Moreover, the children are depending on the income of the petitioner who is the bread earner of the family.
Having considered his avocation and also fate of the children, it is appropriate to grant him bail by imposing suitable conditions.

7. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.18/2023 of respondent Police Station, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9642 (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
